issues.detail: The Greek 'ο ασπασμος' (the greeting) is the subject of the phrase, but the Vietnamese translates it as a noun phrase indicating 'this greeting' (Lời chào này) and then changes the structure to imply the author is writing it ('chính tay tôi... viết'), whereas the Greek text is a fragment 'the greeting [at] my hand of Paul'. Most importantly, the Vietnamese adds 'nầy' (this), which is not in the Greek.
